panel.summary: SSRF via unvalidated image `src` in the CLI slides/docs export fetcher that this change promotes as a shipped feature
panel.evidence: `createImageFetcher` resolves relative srcs against the server base but passes any absolute URL through untouched (image-fetcher.ts:28) and then `fetchImpl(resolved)` with no scheme, host, or private-IP restriction (image-fetcher.ts:49). It is wired into `slides export --format pptx` at packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:207-208 and the docs export paths at packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:269-313. Because deck content accepts arbitrary `data.src` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:337), an attacker who can write to a deck plants `src: "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/"`; when the deck is exported by an automation/CI job on the same network the response bytes are embedded verbatim into the produced `.pptx` media part (packages/slides/src/export/pptx/index.ts:162-165), which the attacker can then read. Pre-existing code, but the change under review documents and advertises this export path (guide/import-export.md "Automating with the CLI").
panel.finding_key: packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts::ssrf via unvalidated image `src` in the cli slides/docs export fetcher that this change promotes as a shipped feature
